text:
Elena (AE): Sam from Vectra asked us to finalize the POC acceptance checklist. They want a 3-week sandbox, regional failover tested, and clear cost & latency gates. Key asks were: p95 latency target, monthly cost cap per 1M request-equivalents, and automated rollback if regional latency spikes. Also they insisted on KMS BYOK and EU-only data residency.

Sam (Buyer): correct. traffic: sustained 26 qps, short bursts to 95 qps; avg input 150 tokens, avg output 80 tokens. Important: we require <20ms cross-region failover time and no more than 5% request loss during failover. Monthly projected ~1.3M req-equivalents.

Noor (SE): thanks. we'll test two regions (eu-west + us-west) and exercise failover during canary. propose acceptance gates that include a regional SLO: primary region p95 <= 260ms; failover latency penalty <= +40ms during the 5min window after switch; successful failover with <=5% error spike.

Ben (Perf Eng): perf test sketch to run (I'll paste to harness):
```
profile: mixed_regional
sustained_qps: 26
peak_qps: 95
p50_seq_len: 170
p95_seq_len: 700
duration: 3h
failover_test: at t=1h simulate region outage for 5m
metrics: p50,p95,p99,error_rate,request_loss_during_failover,token_burn
```
Primary perf gate uses p95 measured in the primary region before and after failover.

Elena (AE): propose the acceptance gates:
1) Performance gate: primary region p95 <= 260ms over a 48h canary, error rate <0.5%. During scheduled regional failover test, request loss <=5% and p95 increase <=40ms for 5m window.
2) Cost gate: modeled monthly burn <= $360 / 1M req-equivalents (we will show both hosted PAYG and dedicated reserved node scenarios). Billing sensitivity to tail tokens and batching window included.
3) Quality gate: evaluation on their 250-example prompt suite: automated F1 drop <= 1.5% and top-1 accuracy within 0.03 of baseline. Customer reserves human review for any borderline cases.
4) Security & residency gate: KMS BYOK validated, EU-only data routing verified, SAML SSO tested, SOC2 summary provided.
5) Failover gate: successful simulated failover with <=5% request loss and confirmation of <20s for traffic steering to complete (we'll measure control-plane and data-plane times).
If any gate fails, automated rollback to baseline model and a postmortem. Who signs each gate? Elena (Redwood AE) to own cost+ops sign-off, Sam (customer) to sign quality & residency, Noor to sign perf/failover results.

Sam (Buyer): ok on signers. for cost gate we want explicit committed-dedicated vs hosted PAYG numbers and a sensitivity table for average seq length +/- 20%. Also need a short appendix describing how you compute "request-equivalents" for mixed gen+RAG payloads.

billing-bot: attached: sample-cost-sheet.csv (internal), tokenization-examples.txt :white_check_mark:

Noor (SE): infra notes: we'll run canary on hosted in eu-west for 24h then provision a dedicated single-node EU pool with burst to 2 nodes. For failover test we'll flip traffic to us-west with the same infra config. We'll include per-region KV-cache warmup time in the report. Also recommend enabling prefix caching for common prompts to reduce tail p95 during failover.

Ben (Perf Eng): technical note: warming KV cache in the target region reduces p95 spike by ~25% on our sim; include two runs: cold-failover and warmed cache. We'll capture per-request timing to measure the 20s traffic steering requirement precisely.

security-bot: attached: soc2-summary.pdf, kms-byok-flow.txt, eu-data-routing-checklist.md :white_check_mark:

Elena (AE): timeline & owners:
- Today EOD: Sam to upload 250-example prompt suite and confirm the maintenance window for failover test.
- +24h: Ben runs perf harness (cold + warmed failover) and posts p95, error-rate, request_loss_during_failover, token_burn.
- +36h: Noor posts infra config and dedicated vs hosted cost scenarios.
- +48-72h: assemble acceptance doc and schedule 30-min sign-off with Sam.
Owners: Ben (perf runs & metrics), Noor (infra config & runbook), Elena (acceptance doc & customer comms), Sam (buyer sign-off).

Sam (Buyer): please make the acceptance doc explicit about rollback contacts and the exact dashboard queries we'll use to verify p95 and request loss. Also confirm the MTTR expectation during the sandbox (we want <30 minutes for rollback and warm recovery).

Noor (SE): will add rollback matrix and the exact API query to compute p95 from our metrics endpoint. We'll target MTTR <30m for traffic rollback and include the warm-retry steps to rehydrate KV caches.

Elena (AE): thanks team 8578; I'll collate and send the draft acceptance doc to Sam for review once benches are posted.
